children: Next's guidance upgrade will prompt debate, but investors will likely be satisfied as the retailer navigates industry headwinds in style, Jefferies analysts say in a note. Management has guided for an 8.4% rise in adjusted pretax profit to 1.255 billion pounds, with consensus at 1.25 billion pounds, as the worse outlook for the U.K. is offset by a stronger performance at its international online division. "Results show all the expected strength of a business growing at an elevated rate, still driven by the combination of modest U.K. progress plus accelerated international expansion," Jefferies says. Shares are up 2.3% at 14,895 pence. (anthony.orunagoriainoff@dowjones.com)
